decisions.reference: Unmodified original A_BrainAwake compiled as host C; original fixed array is exercised only up to its 32-target capacity. Native uses actual actor handles and the owned target table. All 38 result slots match.
scope: Zero through 32 targets in thinker order
Different actor types, retired thinkers, dead active targets and non-actor thinkers
Cursor reset, full-volume awake sound, unchanged random stream and easy phase
Zero, 33, 129 and 257 targets, including native actor-slot growth
Eight repeated refreshes per population with stable heap usage
Dead versus retired targets and generation reuse
Owner/inactive guards leave prior table and cursor unchanged
Sound failure after publication leaves the new table owned and valid
Awake during a thinker action; creation/deletion rejected while thinkers run
A target removed by the sound callback leaves a safely stale generation handle

isolatedHarnesses.scope: Only omit-list changes were made in eight isolated probes. Their included module sequence and complete module-prefix bytes are identical to the baseline; the remaining runner text is identical after removing the new omit token. No duplicate native execution was needed for unchanged inputs.

nativeDesign: Brain owns a target-handle table sized to the current actor population, replacing the original 32-pointer array. C parity is claimed only inside that array capacity; larger populations have separate native ownership tests.
The host may supply a retained easy-mode phase when creating a new level context. Target refresh does not reset it.
Missing/retired handles require bounded handling by the forthcoming spawn-cube action.
remaining: Complete actor dispatcher and persistent native game host
